seoTitle: How to Print a Single Check From QuickBooks Online
metaDescription: Print one check in QuickBooks Online: write it with Print later ticked, run the one-time alignment setup, set the starting check number, and tell QuickBooks whether it printed correctly.
intro:
QuickBooks Online prints checks from a queue. You write the check, mark it to print, and then print whatever you tick in the queue, which can be a single check. There's no separate single-check mode to find.

This guide walks through writing the check, the one-time alignment setup that keeps the amount inside the right box, and the confirmation screen at the end. That last screen matters more than it looks: telling QuickBooks a check printed badly is how it keeps the check in the queue and the numbering straight.
prerequisites: Printable check stock: standard (three checks per page) or voucher (one check per page with stubs)
Adobe Reader installed and set as your browser's PDF viewer, which Intuit lists as a requirement for check printing
A few sheets of plain paper for the alignment test, so you don't waste real checks

steps.heading: Start a new check
steps.body:
Click + Create at the top of the left rail and choose Check from the Vendors column. The same column also lists Print checks, which opens the print queue for checks you've already written, not a blank check. For a new payment, start with Check.

Intuit's current help pages reach the queue through All apps → Expenses & Bills → Expense transactions → Print checks. The Create menu route in the recording still leads to the same place.

image.caption: The Create menu's Vendors column, with Check near the top and Print checks further down.

steps.heading: Fill in payee, account, category and amount
steps.body:
Pick the Payee. If a mailing address is on file it fills in automatically, and that's the address that shows through a windowed envelope. Choose the Bank Account the money comes from; its balance appears beside the dropdown. Set the Payment date.

In the table below, choose a Category for the account the payment posts to and enter the Amount. Add a Description if the category alone won't explain it later. The Total at the bottom should match the large amount at the top right. If they differ, a line is wrong.

steps.heading: Tick Print later
steps.body:
Tick Print later under Check no. The number field changes to "To print", which means QuickBooks assigns the number when the check comes out of the printer. If you type a number yourself and leave Print later unticked, the check won't appear in the print queue.

From here, click Print check at the bottom of the form to print straight away, or Save and close to leave it in the queue and print later.

image.caption: A $1,000.00 check with the Salary category, Print later ticked and Check no. showing "To print".

steps.heading: Run the alignment setup the first time
steps.body:
Before the first real check, open Print checks and select Print setup. Choose voucher or standard to match your stock, then View preview and print sample, and print it on plain paper. Hold the sample over a blank check against a light.

If the text doesn't sit in the boxes, select No, continue setup twice, then drag the grid (or adjust it manually) to line up with your sample. Print again and repeat until it fits, then click Finish setup.

steps.heading: Print the one check
steps.body:
In the print window, make sure the bank account dropdown shows the account you wrote the check from. In Starting check number, enter the number printed on the first check loaded in your printer. Tick only the check you want and click Preview and print, then Print.

When QuickBooks asks how it went, answer honestly. Yes, they all printed correctly removes the check from the queue with that number. Some checks need reprinting asks for the first check number that needs fixing and keeps it in the queue, so you can load a new check and print again. Click Done to finish.

troubleshooting.problem: The check isn't in the Print checks list
troubleshooting.cause: Either Print later wasn't ticked when the check was saved, or the Print checks window is showing a different bank account.
troubleshooting.fix: Switch the account dropdown to the right bank account. If it's still missing, open the check from Expense transactions, tick Print later and save.

troubleshooting.problem: Text prints outside the boxes on the check
troubleshooting.cause: The alignment hasn't been set for this printer and stock, or the PDF viewer or printer driver is scaling the page.
troubleshooting.fix: Rerun Print setup and adjust the grid. If it's still off, Intuit suggests checking the print scale settings in Adobe Reader or your printer's driver.

troubleshooting.problem: The printer jammed or the check came out damaged
troubleshooting.cause: A physical misprint that QuickBooks has no way to detect on its own.
troubleshooting.fix: At the confirmation prompt, choose Some checks need reprinting and enter that check's number. It stays in the queue for a fresh check.

faq.question: Can I print just one check without printing everything in the queue?
faq.answer: Yes. Tick only that check in the print window before you click Preview and print. Unticked checks stay in the queue.

faq.question: What's the difference between Check and Print checks in the Create menu?
faq.answer: Check opens a blank check to write a new payment. Print checks opens the print queue, where checks already saved with Print later ticked wait to be printed.

faq.question: Standard or voucher checks: which do I need?
faq.answer: Match whatever stock you bought. Standard stock has three checks per page; voucher stock has one check per page plus stubs. You pick the type during Print setup.

faq.question: Where does the check number come from?
faq.answer: From the Starting check number you enter in the print window, which should match the number on the first check in your printer. That's why the form shows "To print" until then.
